ACCEPT

The question effectively targets a critical refinement for improving reasoning quality in art history multiple-choice tasks. By pushing for discrimination based on distinctive rather than superficial features, it addresses common pitfalls in art movement identification (e.g., confusing Impressionism and Post-Impressionism based solely on "visible brushstrokes"). This specificity will force the model to leverage deeper art historical knowledge about philosophical intentions, historical context, and unique stylistic innovations, directly enhancing answer accuracy and pedagogical value.
